records.text: Iran has killed and maimed thousands of American soldiers.
records.speaker: Karoline Leavitt

appearances.snippet: They have killed and maimed thousands of American soldiers. And President Trump was not going to allow Iran to attack our bases and our troops and our men and women in the Middle East first.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 49:31. The Pentagon has attributed at least 603 U.S. troop deaths in Iraq to Iranian-backed militias, and public records describe thousands more maimed or wounded across proxy attacks. The combined scale is plausible, but the wording collapses direct Iranian action, proxy responsibility, deaths, injuries, soldiers, and civilians into one imprecise total.

sources.title: Iran killed more US troops in Iraq than previously known, Pentagon says - Military Times
sources.relevance: Reports the Pentagon figure of 603 U.S. deaths tied to Iranian-backed militants and many more wounded, supporting the substance but showing the statement compresses proxy and direct responsibility.

records.text: President Trump launched Operation Epic Fury to prevent Iran from attacking U.S. bases and troops first.
records.speaker: Karoline Leavitt

appearances.snippet: They have killed and maimed thousands of American soldiers. And President Trump was not going to allow Iran to attack our bases and our troops and our men and women in the Middle East first. ... And that's why he took this historic action by launching Operation Epic Fury.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 49:31. Trump ordered Operation Epic Fury, and administration officials, including Rubio and Leavitt, publicly said the preemptive timing was chosen to prevent anticipated Iranian attacks on U.S. troops and bases and reduce casualties.

sources.title: Operation Epic Fury Fact Sheet - U.S. Department of Defense
sources.relevance: Primary government fact sheet states the operation was launched preemptively to counter anticipated Iranian attacks.
